overall: The AG found the School Building Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by approving insufficient January 21 minutes (remote participants, location, presentation summaries, exhibit list), but not on the invoice portion; ordered compliance and amended minutes within 60 days.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the January 21 meeting, as originally approved, did not specify which members participated remotely.
allegations.key_passage: We agree that the minutes failed to specify which members of the Committee participated remotely at the January 21 meeting.

allegations.summary: Minutes of the Approval of Invoices portion were allegedly insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: There was no discussion regarding the purpose or substance of the invoices; therefore, the minutes appropriately do not include such detail.

allegations.summary: Originally approved minutes gave only general subject matter of the Old Business presentations, without summarizing the substance of the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: In creating and approving insufficiently detailed minutes, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Originally approved minutes did not specify the location of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We agree and find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to include the location of the meeting in the minutes.

allegations.summary: Minutes did not include a list of documents and exhibits, such as presentations, used at the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: and these documents and presentations should have been listed in the minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Within sixty (60) days of the letter, further amend the January 21 minutes to include a summary of the Old Business presentations and a list of documents and exhibits used at the meeting.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Furthermore, we order the Committee, within sixty (60) days of the date of this letter, to further amend the minutes of the January 21 meeting, in accordance with the guidance provided above, to include (1) a summary of the presentations delivered in the “Old Business” portion of the meeting and (2) a list of documents and exhibits used at the meeting.
